items.title: The exterior product over a base of dimension one is well defined on Chow groups in degree shifted by one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)

items.difficulty_reason: The statement is that the exterior product map CH_n(X) tensor_Z CH_m(Y) -> CH_{n+m-1}(X x_S Y) over a base of dimension one is well defined (statement lines 14657-14661). The proof first defines the product on cycles: among the pairs (i, j) one keeps only those where X_i or Y_j dominates an irreducible component of S, and shows that these form a locally finite family of closed subschemes of delta-dimension n + m - 1, so that the sum of n_i m_j [X_i x_S Y_j] makes sense (proof lines 14664-14681). Compatibility with rational equivalence is then obtained by splitting the case distinction between components that do and do not dominate S: for an integral X' of dimension n dominating an irreducible component of S, the projection X' -> S is flat of relative dimension n - 1 by the Dedekind domain input, so the composite of the flat pullback with the proper pushforward is a bivariant class whose cap product sends [Y'] to [X' x_S Y']_{n+m-1} (proof lines 14684-14698). For the complementary case, where X' -> X -> S factors through a closed point s of S, the point s is an effective Cartier divisor with trivial normal bundle, so composing the Gysin class of s in S with the flat pullback along the now flat X' -> s of relative dimension n gives a bivariant class whose cap product sends [Y'] to the correct cycle precisely when Y' dominates a component of S and to zero otherwise, matching the definition on cycles (proof lines 14701-14722). Splitting the cycle definition along the two kinds of components and building the matching bivariant class in each case is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
